Question Title: Induction fails! What's wrong with the prisoner's reasoning in the famous paradox (The Unexpected Execution )?
Question Content:
There is a prisoner on death row. His captor 
is especially cruel, and so on a Monday morning 
tells the prisoner: 
"You will be executed later this week. 
However I won't tell you what day beforehand. 
When you are dragged out to the firing squad, 
it will be a surprise to you."
The prisoner mulls this over. The week runs from 
Monday to Sunday. If the prisoner makes it to Sunday, 
there are no further days for the execution to 
take place. It must be that day he will be shot 
but it wouldn't be a surprise. Hence the 
execution cannot be on Sunday and must be on 
Tuesday through Saturday. But then if the prisoner 
makes it to Saturday, there are no further days 
for the execution to take place, as Sunday is no 
longer an option. Hence the execution must be on 
that day, but then it wouldn't be a surprise. 
Thus it cannot take place on Saturday. The reasoning 
continues in a similar fashion until every day 
is ruled out. The prisoner concludes that there is 
no way for the conditions of the execution to 
be fulfilled and therefore the execution cannot 
take place. Therefore, it comes as a great shock 
when on the Thursday the prisoner is taken from his 
cell and placed before the firing squad.

Although many modern therapies can be construed to conform to an allopathic rationale (eg, using a laxative to relieve constipation), standard medicine has never paid allegiance to an allopathic principle. Question Title: Finding the solution to  ln(x)/x = (1/2) ln(2/86400)?
Question Content:
Another person here suggested this problem. 

I used the Newton-Raphson method to find the root of the function f(X)=exp(aX)-X, where a=.5*log(2/86400)=-5.336798 approximately. 

This yields the iteration Xn+1=Xn-f(Xn)/f'(Xn) which converges very rapidly to a value of X=0.25560605642100. Starting at X0=0, after 1 iteration, the estimate is in error by about 9.8e-2, after 2 iterations, the estimate is in error by about 1.5e-2, after 3 iterations the estimate is in error by about 3.5e-4, after 4 iterations the estimate is in error by 1.9e-7 and after 5 iterations it has has converged to an estimate that is in error by 5.6e-14.
